subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB337, LANDED. Both arms are enforced in ONE screen, StatementValidation.CheckIntoReceiver, called from MoveBinder.BindIntoPhrase -- the single site the sequential READ, the keyed READ and the sort RETURN all funnel through (FILES design D23/D24), so a fourth INTO-bearing verb inherits the rule rather than re-deriving it. Arm a) is IntoPhraseRules.AdmitsRecordCount, which carries the ONE per-verb difference: READ's 'no record description entry or only one' admits a record-less FD (13.4.5.3 SR3) where RETURN's 'only one' does not (13.4.6.3 SR2). Arm b) is ItemCategory.IsAlphanumericOrNational over identifier-1 AND every record of the file; its group arm is 13.18.29.4 GR3's alphanumeric group item (all three conjuncts -- no GROUP-USAGE, not strongly typed, not a variable-length group) and its national arm covers both an elementary national item and the GR2 b) national group. A reference-modified or level-66 RENAMES identifier-1 is admitted without reading the underlying entry: 8.4.3.3.4 GR6 makes the unique data item elementary alphanumeric whatever it is described as. Diagnostic COBOL1994. PRE-FIX MEASUREMENT: an FD with '01 REC-A / 05 A-1 PIC X(4)' and '01 REC-B / 05 B-1 PIC 9(4) COMP' read INTO a PIC 9(4) COMP item compiled and printed GOT=0001 on this worktree's own build; it now draws COBOL1994 at all four editions. EDITIONS: all four -- the rule is the 1985 standard's too; the two shapes that make the 2023 wording narrower (an ALPHANUMERIC group item rather than any group item, and category national) cannot be declared below 2002, so one predicate is per-edition-correct by construction and no gate is written. The positive golden ships in all four legs and its case A is the over-reject guard: arm a) admits a category-NUMERIC identifier-1 over a single-record FD, which a screen testing only arm b) would have rejected.
